image_facts.tracking_moving_flag: F (sidereal tracking; comet trail in 15 s = 0.73 arcsec, sub-pixel)

pointing.note: NEOSSat WCS centre sits ~8 arcsec from the SPHEREx field centre: the two telescopes were looking at the same patch of sky that morning.

comet_prediction.method: Linear interpolation of the SPHEREx 5-epoch motion fit (data/motion.json; fit RMS 0.31 arcsec over 2025-12-14) to the NEOSSat mid-exposure time. NEOSSat time falls between SPHEREx epochs 3 and 4, so this is interpolation, not extrapolation.

visibility_assessment.verdict: NOT DETECTED in this single 15.0 s frame
visibility_assessment.control_test: Same aperture measurement at 400 random field positions: the predicted-position excess ranks at the 12th percentile (r=5 px) and 60th percentile (r=8 px) - statistically indistinguishable from empty sky positions.
visibility_assessment.nearest_features: Brightest raw pixel within 15 px of the prediction is 2920 ADU at 12.3 px offset (consistent with noise/star field). A diffuse patch 14.5 px (44 arcsec) away at (484,519) has a profile width (sigma ~4.9 px) matching the stellar PSF in this product (sigma 5.3-6.5 px) and no counterpart at that fixed sky position in SPHEREx epochs 1/5; assessed as a faint field star, not the comet.
visibility_assessment.context: 3I/ATLAS in mid-Dec 2025 was a faint, highly diffuse comet; NEOSSat is a 15 cm microsatellite and this is a single 15 s sidereal-tracked exposure. CADC holds 44 NEOSSat 3I observations overlapping this field from 2025-12-13/14 (data/neossat_check.json); shift-and-stack of that sequence is the natural next step and was out of scope for this single-image task.
